Arjun (arch): Heads up — I'm putting forward a 'module-lattice' proposal for long-term refactor of the enrichment surface. TL;DR: move the core enrichment logic into a small, well-tested library that both the hotpath runtime and a thin legacy shim can call. This reduces service surface + tech debt while keeping a safe fallback for tenants still on the old path. Want quick feedback on tradeoffs and rollout approach. :eyes:
Sara (platform): curious — what do you mean by 'library' vs 'shared service' here? latency/cost implications?
Arjun (arch): Good Q. Library = pure code artifact we publish (semver, CI tests). Hotpath runtime links it directly (in-process) for lowest latency. Shared service = network hop. The shim service is only for legacy consumers that can't upgrade; over time we expect them to migrate to in-process.
Julia (runtime): In-process is ideal for latency but raises ownership questions for KV cache and chunked state. If the same code runs in both contexts we need clear boundaries for cache ownership and lifecycle.
Mike (englead): Also want to call out testing matrix: unit + integration + golden-path evals. We should require the library to run under both instrumented runtime and shim to catch behavioral drift.
Arjun (arch): Agreed. Draft API (very small):
```
package redwood.enrichment.core
func Enrich(ctx, request) -> EnrichedOutput
// config layer keeps runtime-specific adapters: CacheAdapter, IOAdapter
```
Shim service would glue CacheAdapter -> remote-kv, runtime would use local-kv adapter.
Sara (platform): How do we handle versioning? If we push a breaking change to the library, we risk many runtimes.
Arjun (arch): Semver + deprecation window. Also plan a compatibility layer: adapter interfaces stable for 2 majors. Breaking changes go through RFC + migration plan.
Lena (product): From product POV: need to guarantee no behavior regressions in top-100 tenants. Can we gate migrations on evaluation sets?
Mike (englead): Yes — canary + dataset-based QA. Proposed rollout phases:
1) extract library and run tests locally (no consumer change)
2) runtime links library in internal stack (dogfood)
3) enable shim pointing at library for 5% of traffic for legacy consumers
4) run golden-path evals + compare top signals for 24–72h
5) ramp to 50% then full cutover, then deprecate shim over quarters
Julia (runtime): Need telemetry hooks: per-tenant latency histogram, cache hit/miss, token cost delta. Also a fast rollback if latency regresses > 10% vs baseline.
Arjun (arch): Noted. Required metrics: enrich.latency.{p50,p95,p99}, enrich.cache.hit_rate, enrich.token_delta.avg, enrich.error_rate. We'll add a behavioral regression check (diff on eval outputs) that blocks ramp if >2% divergence on golden set.
OpsBot: deploy-checklist created: https://internal/redwood/tasks/ENR-PRUNE-42 (auto)
Sara (platform): One more concern — binary size and startup time if we add library to runtime. Do we have estimates?
Julia (runtime): Rough probe: current runtime binary + enrichment modul adds ~4–6MB compressed, startup +12–20ms cold startup. That's acceptable given cold starts are rare for hotpath. We'll measure.
Mike (englead): Who owns the extraction? Arjun wants arch to own the initial extraction, runtime team to own adapters, platform to own rollout configuration, product to own golden tests.
Arjun (arch): I can own the initial extraction and design. Volunteers for owners: Julia for runtime adapters, Sara for rollout config, Mike to coordinate golden-path QA, Lena to define product checks.
Lena (product): I'll draft the top-100 tenant test and acceptance criteria.
Mike (englead): Timeline suggestion: Q2 spike (2 weeks) for extraction + tests, Q2 sprint for dogfood, Q3 canary + ramp.
Arjun (arch): Sounds good. Action items: Arjun creates RFC + code scaffold by EOW, Julia will run local probe and report startup numbers, Sara will prepare rollout gating dashboard, Mike will outline golden set and test harness.
Sara (platform): +1. I'll add a postmortem template for the cutover in case we need it.
Julia (runtime): I'll run an A/B with local adapter vs remote shim on a synthetic workload and post numbers here.
Arjun (arch): Thanks all. If no objections I'll file RFC today and assign tasks. :thumbsup:
Mike (englead): :+1:
Lena (product): :+1:
